solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Visions of extremely dangerous wrapping paper

indicators.note: wrapping says the outer pair of letters goes around the paper word
extremely asks for the word's extremities, its first and last letters only

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Someone sees visions of hazardous gift-wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' picks D and S from 'dangerous'; 'wrapping' puts them round REAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreams are visions seen in sleep or imagined, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Face-up in a river port in Oz

indicators.note: in places the turned face word inside a river and the letter a

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a dial is a face, as of a clock or slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: Someone floats face-up in a river at an Australian harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIAL to LAID, which goes 'in' A + DEE (the Dee is a British river).
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia and a seaport; Oz is slang for Australia.

clue.text: Appear with garment for equestrian

parts.note: to show up is to appear, so show can mean appear
a jumper is a knitted garment, British for sweater

explanation.surface: A rider turns up wearing a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A JUMPER is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is a rider who competes over fences, so an equestrian in that sport.

clue.text: Eat up, woman!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone tells a woman to finish her food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of 'eat up', but it reverses DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female first name, the kind of name crosswords use for any woman.

clue.text: Rapid growth ruining a coastline

indicators.note: ruining wrecks the arrangement of the letters of a and coastline, so they are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Fast development spoils a stretch of shore.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalation is a rapid increase or intensification, so rapid growth fits.

clue.text: Noble almost missing New York environment

indicators.note: missing says letters are dropped from the word for almost
environment says the dropped letters are the ones surrounding the rest, at either end

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: An aristocrat nearly skips the New York scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing New York environment' removes the N and Y that surround EARL in NEARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, so a noble by rank.

clue.text: Building up quickly before cracking?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
cracking and fab are both informal British words for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether quick construction comes before failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' looks like breaking, but it is British slang for great, as is FAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a building made from factory parts and put up fast, so a quickly erected building.

clue.text: Peerless cast in a 1996 movie

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the word Peerless is rearranged

explanation.surface: An unrivalled cast appears in a 1996 film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the film's actors, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepers is a 1996 film directed by Barry Levinson, so it names that movie.

clue.text: Shark ends recreation for waders

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation, making again, says these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A shark finishes off fun for people in waders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' is read as re-creation: the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Redshanks are wading birds with red legs, so waders in the bird sense.

clue.text: Thirty days for pair getting into trouble

indicators.note: getting into puts the pair abbreviation inside the trouble word

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as an illness does

explanation.surface: Two people get a month's sentence for causing bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty days' reads like a jail sentence, but it defines a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The old rhyme 'Thirty days hath September, April, June and November' lists this month.

clue.text: Acknowledged nothing's been paid?

definitions.meaning: permitted or conceded, as in a point granted in argument
read as two words, every sum still owing

explanation.surface: Someone admits that no bill has yet been settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed means conceded or acknowledged, and split as all owed it means every debt is outstanding.

clue.text: Whole note in jazz standard

parts.note: the whole of something is all of it
me is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A semibreve appears in a well-known jazz tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whole note' looks like the American name for a semibreve, but it is split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: All of Me is a 1931 song that became a much-recorded jazz standard.

clue.text: Runner in the Catskills

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words the Catskills

explanation.surface: Someone races in the Catskill Mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests a person racing, but here it means a sliding blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, a long narrow strip that slides over snow.

clue.text: Cool Scandinavian in a French story

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in places the Scandinavian inside the French article and story

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story
a Lapp is a Sami person of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A calm Scandinavian character appears in a French tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Unflappable means never flustered, so cool in the sense of calm.

clue.text: British infantry regiments in a sort of dug-out?

indicators.note: out, tacked onto dug, says the preceding letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: British soldiers sheltering in a kind of trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug-out' looks like one word, a trench, but its tail 'out' signals the anagram of A SORT OF DUG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Foot Guards are the five infantry regiments of the Household Division, including the Grenadier and Coldstream Guards.

clue.text: Urge a leader to carry on in spite of opposition

definitions.text: carry on in spite of opposition

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: Someone urges a boss to keep going despite resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To press ahead is an idiom for continuing determinedly despite obstacles.

clue.text: Cricket stroke making Surrey opener cry

indicators.note: opener asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A cricket shot makes Surrey's opening batsman burst into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' sounds like an opening batsman (Surrey is a county cricket side) but picks the first letter, S. A sweep is a cross-bat cricket shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweep is a cricket shot played on one knee, sending the ball square or behind on the leg side.

clue.text: German upset about a vehicle somewhere in Georgia

indicators.note: about says the reversed name goes round the other pieces
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A German gets upset about a truck somewhere in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HANS into SNAH, which goes 'about' A + VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Savannah is a port city in the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: Japanese band leaders in Okinawa buying instruments

indicators.note: leaders in asks for the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Japanese musicians in Okinawa purchase instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash, a band of cloth, worn around a kimono.

clue.text: Distinctive spirit of those putting English first

indicators.note: putting, with first later in the clue, says a letter is moved to the front
first says where the moved letter goes: the start of the word

explanation.surface: Patriots who rank England above all have a particular character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting English first' moves the E of THOSE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a group or culture.

clue.text: Innocuous bit of Hellenism like the Venus de Milo

indicators.note: bit of asks for a small piece, the first letter of the word

parts.note: the Venus de Milo is a famous ancient Greek statue missing both arms

explanation.surface: A harmless trace of Greek culture, like the armless statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocuous and harmless are synonyms, both meaning causing no injury.

clue.text: Marshal given secret deputies

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A marshal is told secrets by stand-ins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like an officer, but as a verb it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice-regents act in place of a regent, so they are deputies.

clue.text: Rodent has it in hole

indicators.note: has says the rodent holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a cavy is a South American rodent such as the guinea pig

explanation.surface: A rodent has it in its burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow space, so a hole.

clue.text: Weird spirit

definitions.meaning: odd or peculiar, an informal British sense
a distilled drink made from sugar cane

explanation.definitionFit: Rum is old British slang for strange, and also the spirit distilled from sugar cane.

clue.text: Slough — where gold is found in bulk

indicators.note: is found in puts the gold word inside the bulk word

parts.note: mass means bulk
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: In Slough, a town, gold turns up in large amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the English town but means a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp, and a morass is a bog, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl taking a month before producing short work

indicators.note: before puts the month ahead of the girl's name

parts.note: NOV is the abbreviation for November
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl takes a month to produce a short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a work of fiction shorter than a full-length book.

clue.text: Bird left on boat

parts.note: an ark is a boat, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A bird is left behind on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, such as the skylark.

clue.text: Student of the Sun — chap only half absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed says the half word is taken inside the sun word

parts.note: solar means of the Sun

indicators.note: only half asks for the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A student of the Sun only half takes in a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' gives CH from 'chap', 'absorbed' into SOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or student, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: In duplicate, therefore OK

indicators.note: in duplicate says the word is written twice

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: Something done twice over is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling, just about acceptable, as does OK.

clue.text: Wine waiter finally up and about

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word waiter

explanation.surface: A wine waiter is at last out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine waiter' reads as a sommelier, but the words split: ASTI, then the last letter of 'waiter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means out of bed and moving about.

clue.text: Do health resorts help American author?

parts.note: taken as written
spas are health resorts
SOS is the distress call asking for help

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether spas assist a US writer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dos Passos was an American novelist, author of the U.S.A. trilogy.
